answer: Give every agent one opal token whose play-of-color pattern is registered at enrolment, then require each epoch a co-signed task: the network pairs strangers at random and both complete a small verified job on a knoll workbench, each stamping it with a sable-ink mark tied to their opal. A Sybil farmer's identities only ever pair with each other, so their co-signature graph collapses into a dense clique while honest links spread across the network. Cloned patterns are rejected and a caught clique loses every token at once. Forging a thousand friends costs a thousand real collaborations.
